items.title: 9.8.3 Salts of weak acids and strong bases

blocks.text: The example of a salt of a weak acid and a strong base is sodium acetate: CH3COONa(s) + H2O(l) gives CH3COO-(aq) + Na+(aq). CH3COO- is the conjugate base of the weak acid CH3COOH and reacts with water, CH3COO-(aq) + H2O(l) gives CH3COOH(aq) + OH-(aq). Na+ is the conjugate acid of the strong base NaOH and does not affect the pH. The solution is basic because of the CH3COO- ion.

blocks.prompt: A solution of potassium carbonate is alkaline. Explain why and give the hydrolysis equation (Quick Check 9.5d).
blocks.explanation: K2CO3 gives K+ and CO3 2-. K+ from the strong base KOH does not react, but carbonate is the conjugate base of the weak acid HCO3- and takes a proton from water: CO3 2- + H2O gives HCO3- + OH-. The OH- released makes the solution alkaline.

items: Weak acid + strong base salt (CH3COONa): CH3COO- hydrolyses to CH3COOH + OH-, Na+ does not; the solution is basic.
